findings.where: Screen 5 (Switch on), first sentence and the button
findings.what: The text opens "Press Switch on." but the screen's demonstration has already switched the current on, and the button reads "Switch off" from the first filmed frame (in the code, "Switch on" can never show), so Dan cannot follow the instruction; open with "The current switches on at 50 A." and end with "Switch it off to watch it cool.", keeping the read without it.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Carrying less), then Screen 10 (A hot room)
findings.what: Screen 9 says "In a 40 °C room only 30 °C of headroom is left, so about 43 A will do": it skips the working (30 ÷ 2 = 15 W, then 50 × √(15 ÷ 20)) and gives screen 10's exact answer one screen before the puzzle asks it, so cut that sentence and let screen 10 and its Why teach it.

The lesson's own title idea, conduction, convection and radiation, gets one Book paragraph where radiation is a bare word ("The third way is radiation.") and no screen names any of the three, so jargon goes unexplained and the "still air" layer's two ways out are never said; add a sentence or two, on screen 5 or 11 and in the Book: conduction through the copper and insulation, then convection and radiation from the surface, with radiation as heat carried by infrared that needs no air.

findings.where: Screen 7 (How long it takes), then Screen 8 (Twice the heat capacity)
findings.what: Screen 7's last sentence, "Twice the heat capacity settles at the same 70 °C, twice as slowly", and its second trace give screen 8's answer just before it is asked, so end screen 7 on the 300 J run and let the puzzle find the 600 J one.

τ = thermal resistance × heat capacity and the 63% are just stated, with no link to the curve he knows from Differential equations and from every RC circuit, so trade "How long it takes is a separate question." for "It climbs like a capacitor charging through a resistor." to keep the screen under 90 words.

The screen shows Current, Room, Extra wrap and Fan, but no sentence asks him to try any of them, so after the 43 A sentence goes, add one line such as "Try the fan, or warm the room." with a read that says what each does.

The hot-room factor √(30 ÷ 40) = 0.866 depends only on the temperatures, not on the example cable, so one sentence saying it holds for any cable with a 70 °C limit reckoned at 30 °C would turn the example into the rule behind his Ca table (quote a table value only if the research notes carry it).
"The wrap alone takes 40 °C of the drop. That is well over the 70 °C limit." reads as though the 40 °C is over the limit, so put the limit with the 110 °C sentence instead.

The unit changes from K·m/W to "3 °C per W" with no word on why (one part rather than each metre, and a kelvin of rise is a degree), so one short sentence there or on screen 11 would stop him wondering.

findings.where: Screen 11 (A motor and a heat sink), the motor picture and its key
findings.what: The only air-coloured ring in the motor is the air gap between rotor and stator, yet the key gives that swatch to "air, fan on the shaft", so the key points the eye inward to the wrong air; draw the outside air or give the gap its own colour.

The brief's electrical links are missing: motors take 0.5 to 5 hours to heat, a stopped self-cooled motor cools more slowly because its fan stops (thermal resistance sets the time too), a protection relay's thermal model runs on this same curve, and there is the seawater cooler; screen 11 is the natural home for the motor and relay points, or say where they are deferred.

What sets how fast heat moves (the material, the thickness, the area and the temperature difference, which is Fourier's law in words) appears nowhere, and one sentence ("a thicker layer or a poorer conductor has more thermal resistance, a bigger surface less") would let him use thermal resistance on any new topic.

[^1] sits on an everyday fact (heat leaves your fingers faster into metal), not a value he would look up, and [^2] appears twice, once in the bold takeaway, so drop [^1] from the text and keep [^2] once.

Both speak of pressing "Play", and the description says the motor and heat-sink pictures show "its losses, its thermal resistances and its rise", but the page has a Switch on/off button and screen 11 draws no numbers, only "rise = losses × total", so bring the descriptions into line with the page.

findings.where: Screen 1 (Steel and wood), opening at 360 px light
findings.what: The opening shot shows an almost empty picture (a faint "steel rail" box and an empty thermometer), and the film shows the wooden rail arriving only after about a second, so draw both rails and thermometers at once and animate only the hands, the arrows and the words.

findings.where: Screens 3, 5 and 9, the heat arrows round the cable
findings.what: A fraction of an arrow is drawn faded (at 45 A a ninth arrow at about a tenth strength), and in a still frame it reads as a ghost or a glitch, worst in dark mode, so round to whole arrows once the current stops moving.
The 30rem column sits at the left of a full-width frame with about two-thirds of it empty, and the trace is drawn at phone size, so centre the column or let the picture widen.
"Two rails under a hand, then a loaded cable cut across…" repeats above all 13 screens and costs about five lines at 360 px before each step, so cut it to one short line or show it on screen 1 only.
